decisions.quote: The two main quantitative results from the original paper – the negative correlation between teacher accuracy and student-teacher Hamming distance and the positive correlation between teacher accuracy and student accuracy – were both replicated. Furthermore, the pattern of accuracies across rule types looked similar to that in the original paper, as evidenced by the bar plot. Therefore, I consider this to be a successful replication.

decisions.reason: Two included replication projects target Jordan, Sommers, Bloom, & Rand (2017): jordan2017_2 (Study 4, line 355 and primary report jordan2017_2.html at line 580) was a successful replication (replicated_instructor_code=1, replicated_report_code=1; report concludes 'This project’s results show a successful replication of Study 4 of Jordan 2017'), whereas jordan2017_1 (Study 3, line 354) received replicated_instructor_code=0 (failed), replicated_report_code=0.9, and an adjudicated_replication_code=0.5 on the authors' [0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1] subjective replication success scale (with m1=34.6 (20.6), m2=36.1 (15.8), N=338 vs. original m1=32.07 (15.93), m2=36.15 (15.37), N=451). Blind coding marked the paper cannot_be_determined because its script left any intermediate score without an attached report uncertain, but whether jordan2017_1 (instructor 0, adjudicated 0.5) is classified as mixed or failed, it is not an unqualified success (1), so aggregating Study 3 (jordan2017_1) with the successful replication of Study 4 (jordan2017_2) unambiguously yields a 'mixed' paper-level outcome.
